name: Bukovel-AD

key_facts.label: Networking
key_facts.value: Up to 9 units linked for wide-area coverage

short_role: Ukrainian mobile counter-drone electronic warfare system — detects, tracks and jams enemy UAV control and navigation links.
characteristics: Passive RF detection and direction-finding across 290–6,000 MHz, triangulating a UAV's position without emitting first
Jams UAV control/data links out to ~20 km and can deny GPS/GLONASS/Galileo/BeiDou positioning
Vehicle, trailer or tripod mounted; deploys in about two minutes
Multiple units network into one wide-area detection and jamming array
employment_notes: Sits back from the immediate line to cover a wide arc of airspace rather than a single position, feeding detections into the wider air-defense and EW picture as much as jamming directly. Passive-first detection matters: emitting a jamming signal before you've located a target gives away your own position, so the system listens before it transmits.
contrast_vs_traditional: Traditional EW targeted enemy radios and radar. This generation of EW is built specifically around the drone threat — detecting and denying the control and navigation links a UAV needs to function at all. It also illustrates the doctrine reference's point about decentralized EW procurement: units fielding their own jammers can create overlapping, uncoordinated 'unofficial EW fields' that degrade friendly drone performance as a side effect, which is a real coordination cost of pushing EW capability down to lower echelons.

connections.description: Reports detected and jammed UAV tracks into the wider air picture.
